subject: StarrX pilot: eval onramp, dataset format, and acceptance criteria
messages:
From: Emily Park <emily.park@starrx.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: Alan Lee <alan.lee@starrx.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up from today: pilot scope & eval data

Hi Vanessa —

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. A quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can scope the pilot: 

- Goal: evaluate LLM-assisted discharge summary extraction and short note generation from our EHR snippets. Primary success metric is extraction accuracy and low hallucination on sensitive fields (meds, allergies).
- We attached a small prompt/sample set (starrx_sample_prompts.csv) and a 50-row PII-sanitized sample.

Questions:
1) Which Redwood models do you recommend we try first for this workload (balance of latency/cost vs. accuracy)?
2) What exact dataset format do you need for a proper run? Any schema examples would help.
3) How do you define scoring/acceptance thresholds for an evaluation run?
4) Timeline & next steps — procurement wants a rough time-to-result and required artifacts.

I can loop in procurement (cc) separately but wanted technical confirmation before we prepare the full sanitized export.

Thanks,
Emily Park
Head of ML Ops, StarrX Health AI
emily.park@starrx.ai
Attachments: starrx_sample_prompts.csv

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@starrx.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 17:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today: pilot scope & eval data

Emily — great to chat, and thanks for the sample. Below is a recommended onramp and concrete artifacts we need to run a meaningful, customer-specific eval on Redwood.

1) Model recommendations (start small, scale up):
- redwood-gpt-small-13b-int8 (good balance: <50ms token latency on Dedicated, strong for extraction)
- redwood-llama-33b-q4 (higher-quality fallback for complex context)
- redwood-vicuna-70b-q4 (use for final pass on hard summaries where recall matters)

Start with the 13B int8 model for a baseline run (cost-efficient). If you see systematic failure modes (low recall or hallucinations on medication fields) we'll promote a subset of failing cases to the 33/70B runs.

2) Required dataset format (we've attached a template: redwood_eval_template.jsonl). Please provide sanitized data in JSONL with one record per line. Required keys: id, input, expected; optional metadata: note_source, deid_level. Example line (single-line JSON):
{"id":"case-0001","input":"Patient has HTN, allergies: none. Meds: metoprolol 50mg...","expected":"Allergies: none; Meds: metoprolol 50mg; Diagnosis: HTN"}

We prefer up to 10k rows for initial run; minimum useful size is ~500 examples stratified by difficulty (simple extraction; multi-field; noisy OCR). Aim for: 300 extraction, 150 multi-field, 50 edge cases.

3) Scoring & acceptance criteria (suggested):
- Extraction (structured fields): token-span F1 >= 0.88 OR exact-match >= 0.80 depending on field strictness.
- Summarization/concise note generation: ROUGE-L >= 0.70 and human-rated factuality >= 0.90.
- Hallucination: manual sample audit; hallucination rate <= 2% on sensitive fields for acceptance.

We run automated metrics (exact/partial match, ROUGE) then sample up to 200 cases for manual labeling (binary factuality + notes). If automated + manual combined pass your acceptance thresholds, we consider the model fit acceptable for a pilot.

4) Operational details & timeline:
- Once you upload sanitized JSONL to the shared Drive/S3 link, Redwood runs a dry validation (format checks) within 2 business hours.
- Baseline run (13B): 1-2 business days depending on size (500–5k).
- Escalation runs (33B/70B): additional 1 day once failing-case set is ready.

Next steps from our side: I attached the eval template (redwood_eval_template.jsonl) and a short prompt bank we recommend. Can you confirm:
- who on your side will prepare the full sanitized export?
- whether procurement needs an SOW/PO before we begin?

Command-line run (for reference):
redwood eval run --model redwood-gpt-small-13b-int8 --input s3://starrx/sanitized/redwood_template.jsonl --scorer rouge,f1 --output s3://starrx/results/stx-452-run1

cc'ing Ben for scoring matrix and Tessa for ops coordination.

—Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@starrx.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today: pilot scope & eval data

Thanks Vanessa — quick additions from the scoring team:

- I've attached a scoring_matrix_starrx.xlsx that maps task types to the exact metric and threshold we'll compute automatically.
- For extraction tasks we use span-F1 implemented over normalized tokens (lowercase, strip punctuation). We also compute field-level exact-match for high-sensitivity attributes (allergies, meds).
- For hallucination, we'll run an automated hallucination heuristic (contradiction detection) and then validate with a 200-case human sample. If the automated heuristic shows >4% hallucination we flag for immediate review and possible model escalation.

Operational note: your workload looks like a good candidate for KV caching of prior notes across the same patient visit; if you plan bursty traffic we can enable larger batch sizes and a short latency SLO on Dedicated to reduce per-token cost. We can run a Dedicated trial for the pilot — cost estimate attached in the sheet.

Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
Attachments: scoring_matrix_starrx.xlsx

Emily
